questions.stem: How do particles move in a solid?

options.text: They do not move at all
They move freely around each other
They move quickly in all directions

questions.explanation: In a solid, particles are held in fixed positions by strong forces between them. They vibrate about these fixed positions but do not move to new positions. This is why solids have a fixed shape and volume. It is a common mistake to say particles in a solid do not move - they do vibrate.
